text:
nick: Quick note - saw p95 jumps on host-side parsing during small concurrent spikes. Attaching quick notes.

tara: Which versions and routes?

nick: Replicated on staging with build r2026. Route /generate-heavy shows the issue when client bursts 10-30 concurrent tiny prompts. Flamegraph pins parse_request and stream_chunker.

felix: Kernel-picker trace?

nick: It switches to slow generic kernel when estimated consolidated batch < 3. With streaming framer enabled we get ~3-6 small writev calls per response which together add ~100us. Also kvcache eviction rate increases by ~30% during spikes.

tara: Two quick mitigations: coalesce writes (buffer up to 1KB or flush timer 2ms) and lower kernel min_batch to 2 with a seq_len cap to prefer optimized kernel for short sequences.

perf-bot: scheduling perf/5795-kern-a-b: run A (baseline) vs B (framer-coalesce + kernel-min-batch=2).

infra-bot: FYI, changing min_batch impacts GPU packing heuristics - coordinate with infra before full rollout.

felix: Will run local repro and attach writev/evict traces.

nick: If coalesce alone reduces p95 significantly we can ship hotfix and keep kernel change behind flag.

perf-bot: perf/5795-kern-a-b completed: p95 improved 16% under burst traffic; kvcache evictions down 45%; writev calls per response down 62%.

nick: Great. I'll open PR for coalesce hotfix. Kernel change will be behind runtime flag pending longer perf.

felix: Posted traces in gist. Noted small risk for long seqs - keeping flag.

perf-bot: closing job. artifacts in perf-dashboard/job/5795.
